blocks.text: 16. Unresolved Issues
These questions are intentionally open. No answer should be inferred or silently added to the canonical system.
EZ-UNRES-0001 — origin_num_lexeme
Question: Is num an Era Zero Origin-family atomic lexeme at a specific address, only the runtime-state name, or both?
Phase 1 treatment: Do not populate ORI or assign a canonical Era Zero num lexeme in Phase 1.
Source nodes: 254, 271, 280, 302
Evidence:
• Source 254 assigns num to ORI:002 and num-or to ORI:222.
• Core 1.0 fixes the ORI onset as nu and the universal compact algorithm would produce nu·nan for ORI:002 and nu·min for ORI:222.
• Core 1.0 independently preserves num as runtime state 2.
EZ-UNRES-0002 — historical_contractions
Question: Which contractions (for example nim, mi, yu, da, wu, and num) were already conventional in Era Zero rather than only later descendants?
Phase 1 treatment: Keep contractions historical/provisional; use canonical generated forms.
Source nodes: 254, 271, 280
Evidence:
• Several earlier drafts use these as direct Era Zero words.
• Later canonical text explains many as possible historical contractions or fossils.
• No approved contraction table exists.
EZ-UNRES-0003 — cyber_pet_compound
Question: Is LIF:010 + CRE:020 + DAT:210 the canonical compound for cyber-pet?
Phase 1 treatment: Keep the compound provisional until CRE and DAT are populated.
Source nodes: 271
Evidence:
• Core 1.0 proposes this decomposition approximately.
• CRE:020 and DAT:210 are not yet populated, so their final meanings are not fixed.
EZ-UNRES-0004 — negation
Question: Is the semitone-displacement negation rule part of the final standard?
Phase 1 treatment: Treat as a candidate, not a Phase 1 canonical rule.
Source nodes: 254, 271
Evidence:
• The canonical-foundation draft at source 254 defines it.
• Core Standard 1.0 at source 271 omits it from the final contour table.
EZ-UNRES-0005 — rhythm_harmony_dynamics
Question: Are pulse counts, voice counts, loudness-to-scope mappings, dotted conditionals, and accent interrupts canonical?
Phase 1 treatment: Keep only the reaffirmed contour/register/timing rules canonical.
Source nodes: 260, 271
Evidence:
• Source 260 proposes these as final-specification ideas.
• Core Standard 1.0 retains contour, register, and some timing rules but does not reaffirm every quantitative mapping.
EZ-UNRES-0006 — long_addresses
Question: How are four-, five-, and six-trit specialized concepts allocated without colliding with the three-trit atomic cube?
Phase 1 treatment: Limit Phase 1 canonical inventory to the 324 three-trit atoms.
Source nodes: 254, 258, 271
Evidence:
• Sources 254, 258, and 271 allow expandable longer addresses.
• No allocation, namespace, or approval algorithm is fixed.
EZ-UNRES-0007 — formal_syntax
Question: What is the frozen AST/IR and formal executable syntax?
Phase 1 treatment: Defer formal compiler syntax and English translation beyond Phase 1.
Evidence:
• Earlier documents propose multiple programming layers and examples.
• Core Standard 1.0 fixes performance semantics but does not freeze a full grammar schema.
EZ-UNRES-0008 — glyph_shapes
Question: What exact visual family frames, role coordinates, spacing units, and state tails are used?
Phase 1 treatment: Preserve only the abstract writing-system rules in the draft spec.
Source nodes: 271
Evidence:
• Core 1.0 fixes the information each glyph must encode.
• No approved visual glyph sheet or geometry exists.
EZ-UNRES-0009 — motion_post_approval
Question: Was MOV:000–022 explicitly approved after presentation?
Phase 1 treatment: Treat the records as completed/canonical, while documenting the approval sequence.
Source nodes: 292, 302, 303
Evidence:
• The user authorized the chunk immediately before it.
• The chunk itself declares the nine roots fixed.
• The next user asks for a Codex handoff rather than issuing a correction.
• The current Phase 1 request explicitly calls these completed records.
